stories.headline: Mélenchon officially declares fourth presidential candidacy on TF1
stories.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election on the TF1 evening news on May 3, after LFI elected officials voted for him at a closed-door Paris meeting earlier that day. His campaign website was online within hours. He framed the RN as his 'principal adversary' and insisted he was the strongest candidate to beat Le Pen in a second round.

stories.headline: RN holds May 1 'Fête de la Nation' in Mâcon as Le Pen–Bardella divergences on economic policy surface publicly
stories.summary: The Rassemblement National held its traditional May 1 meeting in Mâcon, with Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella co-headlining before 5,000 supporters. The event was overshadowed by a visible disagreement between the two leaders on taxing TotalEnergies 'superprofits' — Le Pen calling a tax 'normal' while Bardella opposed new levies — and by counter-demonstrations attended by 2,000–3,000 people. Coverage also tracked Le Pen's stated preference for a centrist opponent in the 2027 second round, internal party tensions over candidate succession pending the July 7 court ruling on her ineligibility, and Bardella's widely reported declaration that he would remove the EU flag from the Élysée.

stories.headline: Lecornu pressures TotalEnergies for 'generous' fuel price cap amid Middle East war-driven energy crisis
stories.summary: With fuel consumption in France down sharply and pump prices surging due to the Middle East conflict blocking the Strait of Hormuz, Prime Minister Lecornu publicly called on TotalEnergies to cap prices more generously after the company posted a 51% profit increase in Q1 2026. The government declined to announce direct subsidies, opting for targeted sectoral aid, while TotalEnergies extended its existing cap. Opposition left parties demanded mandatory price freezes or windfall taxes; a CGT open letter called for a 5% SMIC increase.

stories.headline: Lecornu's personal call to a verbalized May 1 baker triggers LFI legal action against the PM
stories.summary: After the government encouraged bakeries to open on May 1, labor inspectors fined an Isère baker for having employees work on the national holiday. Prime Minister Lecornu personally called the baker to assure him no fine would be paid, then staged a bread-buying photo op in Haute-Loire alongside Laurent Wauquiez. LFI filed a complaint to the Court of Justice of the Republic, accusing Lecornu of 'attempting to obstruct the execution of the law.' The episode drew broad criticism from left-wing unions and parties who called him a 'delinquent prime minister.'

stories.headline: Orion 26 high-intensity military exercise concludes; Macron hails European defense signal
stories.summary: President Macron attended the final day of Orion 26 on April 30 at the Mailly-le-Camp and Suippes military camps, observing 12,500 troops and allied forces in France's largest combat exercise since the Cold War. He praised the exercise as 'a clear signal to allies and adversaries' and highlighted drone modernization and European coalition capacity. The Ministry of Armed Forces also conducted an unprecedented civil requisition exercise as part of Orion to test mobilization of civilian transport assets.
